text:
Rasmus Andersson's first full season in Vegas has been hard going on the scoresheet. Daily Hive's headline on Nov. 16: "Ex-Calgary Flames defenceman Rasmus Andersson continuing to struggle with Golden Knights." He has 3 goals and 7 points in 25 games, none on the power play, and two points in his last ten.

Our numbers say a good part of that is bad luck. Vegas has scored 12.4 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, a lot of lost points for a defenseman playing 19.7 minutes a night. His own shooting is right at the league rate for defensemen (6.4%), and our talent range puts his scoring near 1.3 points per 60, against the 0.85 he's posting.

Not all of it is luck. At 5v5 the Golden Knights have 48% of the attempts and 49.6% of the expected goals with him out there, below their level when he sits. The coaches are still leaning on him: 40 blocked shots, and 23.7 minutes in Winnipeg on Nov. 21, his most in ten games.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 215 defensemen at 1.7 wins above replacement. That's the player Vegas traded for.
